image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Standalone single-storey small King Power duty free store building, detailed front elevation with a wide glazed shopfront between cream painted piers under a deep dark navy fascia carrying the King Power wordmark and crown device on an illuminated sign, flush poster lightboxes set into the piers and lit display shelving visible inside, plain warm cream painted side and rear walls in a single flat off-white tone clearly lighter than the background, with a secure service door, flat roof with a low parapet and roof-mounted air-conditioning condensers. The flat roof deck is dark charcoal bitumen waterproofing, clearly darker than the mid-grey background, and the galvanised condenser units sit on it in obvious contact. Materials: dark navy composite panel, cream painted piers and metallic sign lettering at the front, plate glass, flat warm cream painted render on side and rear walls, dark charcoal roof deck with galvanised roof plant.

IMPORTANT: the building is a completely solid closed box. Glazing appears ONLY on the flat front elevation and the shop interior behind it is brightly lit and fully opaque - the background must NOT be visible through any part of the building. The side and rear walls are solid cream render with no windows and no openings; the glazed shopfront does not wrap around the corner. No part of the building may match the background tone.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless MID grey (#6E6E6E). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow. Apart from the building's own signage described above, there is no other text or lettering anywhere in the frame.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Real trademark: King Power. The repo's MIT licence covers this asset's code, not the mark; anyone shipping it needs their own trademark clearance.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.92 -- not a pass self-score. 1540/16000 triangles, 11/12 draw calls, 7/8 materials, 11/16 unique geometries. Second build: roofline, corner wrap, piers, lightboxes, shopfront layout, door and plant all re-authored off three homography-rectified views of the plate.

featureReviews.evidence: Envelope built at 8.00 x 4.60 x 7.00 m (coping 2 cm proud on each face: 8.04 x 7.00, its rear face 5 mm behind the rear upstand). Authored off three homography-rectified views of the plate (scratch/_kp/{front,side,roof}_rect.png): the coping is ONE level all round at 4.44..4.60, on the band at the front and on the cream walls at the sides, exactly as the plate's roofline reads; the deck is a shallow well 0.35 m down and the two units stand above the coping to 5.005 m (8.8% on one axis, on plant, inside the 10% tolerance).
featureReviews.notes: Second build. The first build had a 0.9 m cream parapet ABOVE the navy band and a deep roof well the plate does not show, and clipped the corner wrap 0.5 m short of the coping. Residual: Meshy still reads this plate 17% shorter than the shared 8.0 x 4.6 x 7.0 module, which is the kit's declaration across seven siblings and wins.

featureReviews.evidence: White KING POWER (2.95 m span, cap 0.38 m, centred at x +0.05) under the gold crown (over the I/N at x -1.05) on slate navy #3A4254 (PBR confidence 0.831) -- BAKED from Nano Banana 2 edits of the plate's own sign crops (sign/nb-word.png, nb-crown.png), laid out at the rectified plate positions in a 2048 x 1024 atlas that also carries the two lightbox poster faces cut from the rectified plate. Faint composite-panel joints at 1.30 m pitch in the band.
featureReviews.notes: The generated lettering is letter-spaced wider than the plate's (ink aspect 8.66 vs 6.5) and is squeezed to 0.90 of natural to hold the plate's span; the crown is the real three-point mark.

featureReviews.evidence: Slate-navy band 3.08..4.43 across the whole front (plate #363B49 on the wrap, #525B64 on a lit panel; authored between them at saturation 0.31), wrapping the front-right corner 1.20 m onto the +X wall at its OWN height up to the coping, as the rectified side shows (wrap x 0..1.2 m).
featureReviews.notes: The first build's #1D2437 rendered the frame at luma 23; this one renders the band at ~#262c3e in shade and ~#3a4050 lit against the plate's #363B49. The corner wrap is 3 cm proud of the side upstand with its front end buried in the band.

featureReviews.evidence: Navy frame at the rectified plate positions: stiles x -2.57 / 3.02, mullions -1.48 / 2.17, door jambs -0.35 / 1.09 with two sliding leaves meeting at 0.38 (mid and bottom rails), head rail 2.72..2.82, transom 2.36..2.44, sill 0.32..0.42 over a granite stall riser to 0.37 and a 0.15 m kerb; between two CREAM PIERS (1.34 m left, 0.86 m right) under a cream lintel 2.80..3.08, each pier carrying a proud lit poster lightbox 0.62 x 1.30 m with a galvanised frame. The pane is a cool light tint at opacity 0.55 over a warm-white backdrop slab, rendering as a lit-shop wash at luma ~187.
featureReviews.notes: The plate's interior (white shelving, display cases) is not modelled and no interior image is projected -- a flat photograph on a flat pane has no parallax. The glass reads as a lit shop rather than as the plate's transparent view; that is the residual.

featureReviews.evidence: Grey granite coping (#7C7F82, plate #7D8285 at the near corner, PBR confidence 0.777) at ONE level 4.44..4.60 on all four faces, 2 cm proud of every parapet face, with a dense speckle tile; the same granite carries the kerb, the stall riser and the service-door reveal.
featureReviews.notes: The plate's coping top face reads a shade lighter than its front; one tone is used.
